anti_sludge_detection_policy.build_cue_routing: If the durable fix is out of lane, finish the direct task and park a Build Cue candidate.
context_rediscovery_patterns: large repo scans when generated read-models answer the question
re-reading stale prompts instead of current contract/readback state
manual Mac/PC relay prompts repeated without post-office metadata
anti_sludge_detection_policy.deterministic_alternative_hint: Prefer receipt/readback, schema validation, token refs, and generated read-models before model retries.
excessive_model_call_patterns: model retries replacing deterministic parser or validator
new agent packet where a local fixture test would prove the boundary
summarization churn without a saved read-model
fake_progress_patterns: readiness report that does not name a receipt, state row, artifact, or blocker
screen closeout that does not reflect backend readback
claimed generated artifact without file path and hash
hardcoded_path_patterns: Mac-only path embedded in backend contract
client-specific Coupa or AP assumption in reusable layer
C-drive artifact writes from WSL backend
anti_sludge_detection_policy.next_safe_move: Use this policy in reviews and future Work Terrain cues; do not activate a live detector here.
one_off_prompt_glue_patterns: bespoke shuttle instructions repeated after a registry exists
custom capture packet with UI-only fields
hardcoded client route leaking into generic framework code
raw_pii_risk_patterns: raw private body in generated JSON
public raw hash of sensitive value
credential, cookie, token, bank, tax, or remit data in normal read-model
retry_loop_patterns: same missing fact requested repeatedly without durable capture
same validation failure retried without narrowing input
agent handoff restarts from scratch instead of using a context packet
sludge_patterns: repeated bespoke shuttle prompts where a registry can help
one-off hardcoded rails where a reusable contract is cheap
broad scans instead of bounded read-model use
compute-saving analysis that itself burns unnecessary compute

gravity_contract.anti_sludge_policy: Detect retry loops, fake progress, one-off prompt glue, broad rediscovery, and hardcoded rails; route durable fixes to Build Cue.
gravity_contract.build_cue_integration_policy: Future work should land as Build Cue or Work Terrain candidates, not hidden live scope expansion.
gravity_contract.compounding_opportunity_policy: Compounding paths may be noted, guarded, or parked only when they are cheap, bounded, and do not slow the direct task.
gravity_contract.compute_efficiency_policy: Use qualitative work-per-watt posture unless measured; avoid fake numeric energy claims.
doctrine: Complete the immediate operator task first.
Do not hijack, moralize, shame, rank, or manipulate.
When a useful reusable rail is cheap and safe, preserve it or park a Build Cue candidate.
Prefer deterministic local rails over repeated model churn.
Convert future opportunities into optional Build Cue or Work Terrain candidates, not active scope creep.
Compute Commons is future opt-in only and default off.
gravity_contract.immediate_task_policy: The current operator task remains the lane unless the operator changes it or a hard safety boundary blocks it.
gravity_contract.next_safe_move: Review the contract, then wire future Build Cue integration only after an explicit lane asks for it.
non_goals: no runtime, queue, or tool execution
gravity_contract.operator_sovereignty_policy: The operator can keep a task one-off. Suggestions must be optional and written in plain ELIOPERATOR language.
gravity_contract.opt_in_compute_commons_policy: Future idle compute assistance is default off, consent-gated, resource-capped, private-data-free, and audit-receipted.
gravity_contract.privacy_policy: Protected values remain tokenized or referenced. Raw private bodies, credentials, and protected material stay out of normal read-models.

opt_in_compute_commons_concept.consent_policy: Explicit opt-in required for the program and for workload class; operator can decline, pause, or stop.
opt_in_compute_commons_concept.description: Future ships or devices may voluntarily offer bounded idle compute for mission-aligned workloads after explicit review.
opt_in_compute_commons_concept.eligibility_policy: Candidate must be safe, described plainly, able to run without private local data, and reviewed before any execution design.
forbidden_uses: weaponization or autonomy-sensitive compute without strict refusal or review
unbounded thermal, battery, network, disk, or user-activity impact
opt_in_compute_commons_concept.mission_alignment_policy: Workload must have a clear operator-approved mission or public-good purpose.
opt_in_compute_commons_concept.next_safe_move: Keep this as a scout contract until a future explicit design lane exists.
opt_in_compute_commons_concept.operator_visibility: Operator must see what would run, why, under what caps, and how to stop it.
opt_in_compute_commons_concept.opt_out_policy: Operator can opt out or pause any future commons participation at any time.
opt_in_compute_commons_concept.privacy_boundary: Default no access to private local data, credentials, cookies, tokens, private documents, or protected stores.
opt_in_compute_commons_concept.resource_boundary: Resource caps, thermal limits, battery limits, user-activity limits, disk limits, and network limits are mandatory before runtime exists.
opt_in_compute_commons_concept.workload_safety_policy: No hidden compute, mining, spam, fraud, surveillance, malware, or autonomy-sensitive work without strict refusal or review.

purpose: Define Meaningful Work Gravity as a bounded compass and model a future opt-in Compute Commons scout.
